idea.body: Any shape with straight sides can be split into triangles, and every triangle's area is half of base times height. A parallelogram's area is base times height, since a triangle cut from one end and moved to the other turns it into a rectangle. A trapezoid's area is the average of its two parallel sides, times the height, since it splits into a triangle and a parallelogram. A rhombus's diagonals cross at right angles, so its area is half of their product. A regular polygon's area is half its perimeter times its apothem, the distance from the center straight out to a side. A garden bed shaped like a rectangle with a triangular roof on top has area equal to the rectangle's area plus the triangle's area.

figure.alt: A rectangle 6 by 3 centimeters with a triangle of height 2 centimeters on top.

workedExample.prompt: A kite-shaped sail is a rhombus with diagonals 14 meters and 10 meters. A support strut runs along a trapezoid brace below it, with parallel sides 8 meters and 4 meters and height 3 meters. Find the total area of the sail and the brace together, in square meters.
steps: The rhombus's area is half the product of its diagonals: 14 times 10 / 2 = 70.
The trapezoid's area is half the sum of its parallel sides, times its height: (8 + 4) times 3 / 2 = 18.
Add the two areas together: 70 + 18 = 88.
The total area is 88 square meters.

figure.alt: A rhombus with diagonals 14 and 10 centimeters.

ways.name: Split into shapes you know
ways.when: Use this when a figure is not one plain shape, like a rectangle with a triangle on top.
steps: A garden bed is a rectangle 8 meters by 5 meters with a triangle roof of height 3 meters.
The rectangle's area is 8 times 5, which is 40 square meters.
The triangle's area is half of base times height: 8 times 3 / 2 = 12 square meters.
Add the two areas together: 40 + 12 = 52.
The total area is 52 square meters.
ways.example: A rectangle 8 meters by 5 meters has a triangle roof of height 3 meters on top. Find the total area.
ways.trap: Forgetting to take half of the triangle's area and using the full base times height.

figure.alt: A rectangle 8 by 5 meters with a triangle of height 3 meters on top.

ways.name: Match the shape to its formula
ways.when: Use this when you can name the shape right away, like a trapezoid or a parallelogram.
steps: A trapezoid has parallel sides 10 centimeters and 6 centimeters, and height 4 centimeters.
A trapezoid's area is the average of its two parallel sides, times its height.
Average the parallel sides: (10 + 6)/2 = 8.
Multiply by the height: 8 times 4 = 32.
The area is 32 square centimeters.
ways.example: A trapezoid has parallel sides 10 centimeters and 6 centimeters, and height 4 centimeters. Find its area.
ways.trap: Adding the parallel sides but forgetting to divide by two before multiplying by the height.

figure.alt: A trapezoid with parallel sides 10 and 6 centimeters and height 4 centimeters.

frames.caption: Area is average of sides, times height

ways.name: The regular polygon as triangles around the center
ways.when: Use this for a regular polygon when you know its side length and its apothem.
steps: A regular hexagon has 6 sides of 4 centimeters each, and an apothem of 2 sqrt(3) centimeters.
Split the hexagon into 6 congruent triangles meeting at the center.
Each triangle has base 4 centimeters (a side) and height 2 sqrt(3) centimeters (the apothem).
The whole area is half the perimeter times the apothem: half of (6 times 4) times 2 sqrt(3).
Half of 24 is 12, and 12 times 2 sqrt(3) is 24 sqrt(3).
ways.example: A regular hexagon has 6 sides of 4 centimeters each and an apothem of 2 sqrt(3) centimeters. Find its area.
ways.trap: Using the side length instead of the apothem as the triangles' height.

figure.alt: A regular hexagon with side 4 centimeters split into six triangles from its center.

frames.caption: Split into six triangles from center
Each triangle: base 4, height the apothem

ways.name: Enclose then subtract
ways.when: Use this for a rhombus when you know both diagonals and want to see why the formula works.
steps: A rhombus has diagonals 12 meters and 9 meters.
Draw a rectangle around the rhombus using the two diagonals as its width and height.
The rectangle's area is 12 times 9, which is 108 square meters.
The four corner triangles cut off exactly half the rectangle, so the rhombus is the other half.
Half of 108 is 54.
ways.example: A rhombus has diagonals 12 meters and 9 meters. Find its area.
ways.trap: Forgetting to take half of the rectangle's area and using the full 108 as the answer.

figure.alt: A rhombus inscribed in a rectangle formed by its two diagonals, 12 by 9 meters.
